title: Comparing and ordering integers
competency: Compare and order integers using a number line, and find the successor and predecessor of an integer.

keywords.def: a > b: a is to the right of b on the number line.
a < b: a is to the left of b on the number line.
The integer that comes just after a given integer: add 1.
The integer that comes just before a given integer: subtract 1.
From the smallest to the largest.
From the largest to the smallest.

en.text: On a number line, the number further right is bigger. Every negative integer is less than 0 and less than every positive integer. For two negatives, the one closer to 0 is bigger, so minus 94 is greater than minus 100.

screens.title: Coldest city
screens.ask: In October, Debre Birhan was −4 °C, Addis Ababa 4 °C and Adama 10 °C. Which city was coldest?
screens.after:
The coldest city has the lowest temperature.
−4 °C is below zero. 4 °C and 10 °C are above zero.
On the number line −4 is furthest left, so it is the smallest.
So Debre Birhan was the coldest.

screens.title: Right is bigger
screens.ask: Tap the points from left to right.

screens.title: To compare integers
paras: Draw a number line and mark the numbers.
The number to the right of the other is bigger.
The number to the left of the other is smaller.
a > b means a is greater than b. a < b means a is less than b.

screens.title: Note
paras: Every negative integer is less than 0.
Every negative integer is less than any positive integer.
−94 is to the right of −100, so −94 > −100.

screens.title: Key words
defs: a > b: a is to the right of b.
a < b: a is to the left of b.

screens.why:
Picture the number line.
−4 is 4 steps to the left of 0.
The number further left is smaller.
So −4 < 0. Every negative integer is less than 0.

Both numbers are negative.
For negatives, the one further from 0 is further left.
−1200 is 1200 steps from 0; −74 is only 74 steps.
So −1200 is further left: −1200 < −74.
Careful: 1200 > 74, but −1200 < −74.
screens.clue: For negatives, further from 0 means smaller.

screens.why:
Both numbers are negative.
−340 is 340 steps from 0; −341 is 341 steps.
−340 is closer to 0, so it is further right.
So −340 > −341.

screens.ask: Compare on the number line: mark −4 and −1. The one further right is greater.
screens.why:
−4 is 4 steps left of 0. −1 is 1 step left of 0.
−1 is further right than −4.
So −1 > −4, even though 4 > 1.
screens.clue: Negative numbers go to the left of 0. Count the steps from 0.

screens.text: Integers between two numbers: tap every integer between −2 and 3.
screens.why:
Count from −2 up to 3: −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3.
"Between" leaves out the two ends, −2 and 3.
So the integers between are −1, 0, 1, 2.
screens.clue: "Between" does not include the end numbers.

screens.text: Solve the inequality: if −5 > x and x is an integer, tap every possible value of x.
screens.why:
−5 > x means x is less than −5.
Less than −5 means to the left of −5 on the number line.
−6 and −9 are to the left of −5, so they work.
−5 is not less than itself. −4 and 0 are to the right.
So x can be −6 or −9.
screens.clue: x is to the left of −5.

en.text: The successor of an integer comes just after it: add 1. The predecessor comes just before it: subtract 1. The successor of minus 4 is minus 3, and the predecessor of 0 is minus 1.

screens.title: One step right
screens.after: One step right of −4 is −3. It comes just after −4.

screens.title: Successor and predecessor
paras: The successor of an integer comes just after it: add 1.
The predecessor comes just before it: subtract 1.
Tap the numbers below to see both.

screens.why:
The successor comes just after: add 1.
−16 + 1 = −15.
On the number line: one step right of −16 is −15.
Careful: −17 is the step to the left, the predecessor.

The predecessor comes just before: subtract 1.
−77 − 1 = −78.
On the number line: one step left of −77 is −78.

The successor is one step right: add 1.
−999 + 1 = −998.
−998 is closer to 0 than −999, so it is bigger. ✓

screens.ask: Successor and predecessor together: what is the predecessor of the successor of −50? ___
screens.why:
Do the inner part first.
The successor of −50 is −50 + 1 = −49.
The predecessor of −49 is −49 − 1 = −50.
One step right, then one step left, brings you back to −50.

en.text: Ascending order goes from the smallest to the largest. Descending order goes from the largest to the smallest. Negatives come first in ascending order, with the one furthest from zero first.

screens.title: Who goes first?
screens.ask: Which comes first in ascending order: −40 or −8?
screens.after:
Ascending order goes from the smallest to the largest.
Both numbers are negative.
−40 is 40 steps from 0; −8 is only 8 steps.
−40 is further left, so it is smaller and comes first.

screens.title: Ordering
paras: Ascending order: from the smallest to the largest.
Descending order: from the largest to the smallest.

screens.title: Put in ascending order
steps: Negatives first. Furthest from 0 is smallest: −40.

screens.title: Read the line from left to right

points.info: Furthest left: the smallest. It comes first.
Furthest right: the largest. It comes last.

screens.ask: Tap the points from left to right. That is ascending order.

screens.title: Key words
defs: From the smallest to the largest.
From the largest to the smallest.

screens.text: Tap them in ascending order (smallest first).
screens.why:
Negatives come first. The one furthest from 0 is the smallest.
−78 is further from 0 than −24, so −78 comes first.
Then 0, then the positives from small to big: 17, 71.
So −78 < −24 < 0 < 17 < 71.

screens.text: Tap them in descending order (largest first).
screens.why:
Descending means largest first.
Positives first: 69, then 59.
Then negatives, closest to 0 first: −9, then −89, then −99.
So 69 > 59 > −9 > −89 > −99.
screens.clue: Largest first. For negatives, closest to 0 first.

screens.why:
Four numbers are negative; 50 is positive, so it goes last.
For negatives, the one furthest from 0 is the smallest.
400 > 350 > 230 > 157, so −400 comes first, then −350, −230, −157.
So −400 < −350 < −230 < −157 < 50.
screens.clue: The negative furthest from 0 is the smallest.

screens.text: Compare scores: final scores are Abebe +2, Almaz 0, Hailu −5, Derartu +3. Who won?
screens.why:
The winner has the greatest score.
On the number line the greatest is furthest right.
Order: −5 < 0 < +2 < +3.
So Derartu (+3) won.

screens.text: Order integers: tap all nine in descending order (largest first).
screens.why:
Descending: largest first.
Positives from largest: 101, 21, 1.
Then negatives from closest to 0: −1, −5, −51, −69, −81, −101.
So 101 > 21 > 1 > −1 > −5 > −51 > −69 > −81 > −101.
screens.clue: Positives from largest; then negatives from closest to 0.

screens.title: Signs
steps: Numbers below zero get a minus sign: 5 °C below zero is −5.
Numbers above zero are positive: +5 or just 5.
On a number line, negatives are left of 0.

screens.text: Write the temperature with a sign: 3 °C below zero is written
screens.why:
Below zero means less than 0.
Numbers less than 0 get a minus sign.
So 3 °C below zero is −3.

items.text: Compare integers: which sign is correct? −150 ? 0
items.why:
−150 is a negative integer.
Negatives are to the left of 0.
Every negative integer is less than 0.
So −150 < 0.

items.text: Compare integers: which sign is correct? −34 ? 34
items.why:
−34 is left of 0 and 34 is right of 0.
A negative integer is less than any positive integer.
So −34 < 34.

items.text: Compare integers: which sign is correct? −23 ? −23
items.why:
Both sides are the same number, −23.
They sit on the same point of the number line.
So −23 = −23.

items.text: Compare integers: which sign is correct? −120 ? −80
items.why:
Both numbers are negative.
−120 is 120 steps from 0; −80 is 80 steps.
−120 is further from 0, so it is further left and smaller.
So −120 < −80.
items.clue: For negatives, further from 0 is smaller.

items.text: Position on the number line: which number is to the right, −1005 or −105?
items.why:
Both numbers are negative.
−105 is 105 steps from 0; −1005 is 1005 steps.
−105 is closer to 0, so it is further right.
So −105 is to the right (and −105 > −1005).

items.text: Integers between two numbers: tap every integer between −98 and −95.
items.why:
Count from −98 to −95: −98, −97, −96, −95.
Leave out the two ends, −98 and −95.
So the integers between are −97 and −96.
items.clue: Between does not include the ends.

items.text: Integers between two numbers: how many integers lie between −10 and −9?
items.why:
−10 and −9 are next to each other: −10 + 1 = −9.
There is no whole step between them.
So no integer lies between −10 and −9.
items.clue: Is there a whole step between them?

items.text: Reading a number line: the points are y, z, 0, m, x, n from left to right. Which is true?
items.why:
On a number line, left is smaller.
z is to the left of x, so z < x.
z > x is wrong for the same reason.
m is to the left of x, so m < x, not m > x.

items.ask: Negative integers: what is the greatest negative integer? ___
items.why:
The negative integers are −1, −2, −3, …
The greatest one is furthest right, closest to 0.
That is −1.
Careful: 0 is not negative.

items.text: Integers: what is the greatest integer?
items.why:
Take any integer, for example 1,000,000.
Add 1: 1,000,001 is bigger.
This works for every integer, so the line never ends.
There is no greatest integer.

The successor comes just after: add 1.
20 + 1 = 21.

The successor comes just after: add 1.
999 + 1 = 1000.

The predecessor comes just before: subtract 1.
−999 − 1 = −1000.
One step left of −999 is −1000.

The predecessor comes just before: subtract 1.
−1000 − 1 = −1001.
One step left of −1000 is −1001.

items.text: Order integers: tap in descending order (largest first).
items.why:
Descending: largest first.
Positives first: 400, then 200.
Then negatives from closest to 0: −300, −445, −757.
So 400 > 200 > −300 > −445 > −757.

items.ask: Integers in a game: Hailu lost 3 baskets, then lost 2 more. His final result is ___
items.why:
A loss is negative: −3, then −2.
Add them: −3 + (−2).
Two losses make a bigger loss: 3 + 2 = 5.
So his final result is −5.

items.text: Compare scores: final results are +2, 0, −5, +3. Who was the loser?
items.why:
The loser has the smallest score.
The smallest is furthest left on the number line.
Order: −5 < 0 < +2 < +3.
So Hailu (−5) was the loser.

test.why:
−8 is left of 0; 2 is right of 0.
A negative integer is less than any positive integer.
So −8 < 2.

The predecessor comes just before: subtract 1.
0 − 1 = −1.
One step left of 0 is −1.

Both numbers are negative.
−250 is 250 steps from 0; −180 is 180 steps.
−250 is further from 0, so it is further left and smaller.
So −250 < −180.

Negatives first, furthest from 0 first: −12, then −7.
Then 0.
Then positives from small to big: 3, 15.
So −12 < −7 < 0 < 3 < 15.

test.text: Integers between two numbers: tap every integer between −4 and 1.
test.why:
Count from −4 to 1: −4, −3, −2, −1, 0, 1.
Leave out the two ends, −4 and 1.
So the integers between are −3, −2, −1, 0.
